name: Seven-spotted ladybug
title: Beneath the spots
overview: Lift a spotted wing cover to discover the folded flight wing underneath.

uc: UC IPM · Identifying the seven-spotted lady beetle
fold: Saito et al. · Wing folding in the seven-spotted ladybird
bell: Bell et al. · Dissection and micro-CT of the seven-spotted ladybird
gut: Pradhan · The alimentary canal of C. septempunctata
beetle: Arizona State University · Tiger beetle anatomy

parts.name: Head capsule
parts.short: The head holds the eyes, feelers, and chewing mouth.
parts.detail: The hard capsule encloses the front of the nervous system. Lift it to see where signals from the eyes and antennae meet.

parts.name: Shoulder shield
parts.short: This dark shield sits just behind the ladybug’s head.
parts.detail: The pronotum covers the first thoracic segment. Its pale patches help distinguish this species.

parts.name: Abdominal back plates
parts.short: These plates lie under the folded wings and cover the soft organs.
parts.detail: The abdominal plates can move relative to one another. The living beetle uses abdominal movements while folding the hindwings.

parts.name: Belly plates
parts.short: These plates protect the underside of the ladybug.
parts.detail: The cuticle is the outer skeleton. The plate edges show where neighbouring body segments meet.

parts.name: Left wing cover
parts.short: Lift the spotted cover to find a thin flying wing tucked underneath.
parts.detail: Each cover is a hardened front wing. Its inside surface helps guide the soft hindwing into folds as the beetle packs it away.

parts.name: Left flight wing
parts.short: This thin wing unfolds into a much bigger flying surface.
parts.detail: Stiffened veins support the membrane in flight. Several folds let the wing fit under a much shorter cover. The animation simplifies the sequence seen on high-speed film.

parts.name: Left compound eye
parts.short: Many tiny lenses gather little pieces of the view.
parts.detail: Each facet admits light to a visual unit. The facets in this model are enlarged so you can see the pattern.

parts.name: Left feeler
parts.short: A ladybug uses its feelers to sample the world around it.
parts.detail: The joints carry sensory structures. Compare the wider club at the tip with the narrower segments near the base.

parts.name: Left chewing jaw
parts.short: These jaws meet from the sides to bite food.
parts.detail: An adult seven-spotted ladybug eats soft-bodied prey including aphids. Paired mandibles work beside the other mouthparts.

parts.name: Left mouth feeler
parts.short: This tiny feeler helps examine a bite of food.
parts.detail: The paired palps sit close to the jaws. Their sensory surfaces sample food as it passes into the mouth.

parts.name: Left front leg
parts.short: Follow this jointed leg from the body down to the foot.
parts.detail: Three pairs of legs attach to the thorax. The long femur and tibia act as levers when muscles pull across a joint.

parts.name: Left front foot
parts.short: Look for the curved claws at the very end.
parts.detail: The foot has small segments and gripping surfaces. The separate claws help the beetle catch on uneven surfaces.

parts.name: Food passage
parts.short: Start here to follow a bite from the mouth into the body.
parts.detail: The foregut carries food toward the midgut. Its entrance lies between the mouthparts and below the brain.

parts.name: Food grinder
parts.short: Food passes through this muscular chamber on its way into the midgut.
parts.detail: This part sits between the narrow food passage and the wider midgut. You can see the change in width in the published dissection.

parts.name: Digesting tube
parts.short: Food breaks down here and nutrients pass into the body.
parts.detail: This winding tube provides space for digestion and absorption inside a very short animal.

parts.name: Rear gut
parts.short: The last stretch takes water back from the food leftovers.
parts.detail: The hindgut leads toward the rear opening. The waste-removal tubes connect near its junction with the midgut.

parts.name: Last gut chamber
parts.short: This is the last chamber before waste leaves the body.
parts.detail: Follow the hindgut to this wider chamber at the back of the abdomen. It is visible in the dissected alimentary canal.

parts.name: Waste-removal tubes
parts.short: These fine tubes help clean the fluid inside the beetle.
parts.detail: Dissections of this species show long looping tubules closely associated with the gut. The loops here summarize their path.

parts.name: Air tubes
parts.short: Follow the branching tubes that bring air close to body tissues.
parts.detail: Air enters through openings in the body wall. The branching network reaches tissues directly. Only the larger paths are illustrated.

parts.name: Breathing openings
parts.short: Air enters the beetle through small openings along its sides.
parts.detail: The openings connect the outside air with the tracheal system. Their rims are enlarged in this teaching model.

parts.name: Heart tube
parts.short: A long tube near the back moves body fluid forward.
parts.detail: The abdominal heart and the forward aorta form the dorsal vessel. The fluid circulates through the open body cavity.

parts.name: Brain
parts.short: Signals from the eyes and feelers arrive here.
parts.detail: The paired optic lobes connect the brain with the eyes. Nerve connections pass around the front of the gut.

parts.name: Nerve cord
parts.short: This line of nerve centers runs along the belly side.
parts.detail: Groups of nerve cells called ganglia help coordinate movement. Their spacing and fusion vary among insects.

parts.name: Flight muscles
parts.short: Bundles inside the chest supply power for flight.
parts.detail: The bundles are shown as simplified groups so you can see how much of the thorax is devoted to movement.

parts.name: Left egg-making tubes
parts.short: Eggs grow in little groups of tubes.
parts.detail: An adult female has paired ovaries. Developing eggs vary in size along the ovarioles. Their number varies with reproductive condition.

parts.name: Right egg-making tubes
parts.short: Eggs grow in little groups of tubes.
parts.detail: An adult female has paired ovaries. Developing eggs vary in size along the ovarioles. Their number varies with reproductive condition.

parts.name: Egg passage
parts.short: Eggs travel down these tubes on their way out.
parts.detail: The two lateral ducts join a common duct. Trace the branches back to the ovaries on either side.

parts.name: Energy stores
parts.short: These soft lobes store supplies the ladybug can use later.
parts.detail: Researchers found well-developed fat bodies in overwintering seven-spotted ladybirds. Their size changes with the animal’s condition.

actions.name: Walk
actions.note: Follow one foot as it lifts, swings forward and touches down.

actions.name: Unfold wings
actions.note: The spotted covers lift first. The thin flight wings unfold beneath them.

actions.name: Fly and land
actions.note: Watch the hindwings beat, then fold back beneath the covers after landing.
